summary: This RFC proposes a set of RFCs on how networking code is integrated into various operating systems, a topic the authors felt had been under-documented. It asks for comments and suggestions.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 967 proposes collecting descriptions of how networking software was integrated with different operating systems. The author invites implementers to contribute essays to a new RFC subseries.

subtitle: A proposal for collecting accounts of networking code integration in operating systems.

tldr.problem: The memo says the networking literature had not sufficiently documented how networking software was integrated into operating systems.
tldr.mechanism: It proposes a subseries of RFCs with essays describing host protocol interpreters, subnet processor interfaces, Telnet, FTP, and relevant operating-system details.
tldr.outcome: The author asks volunteers to document major and minor operating systems and offers to coordinate submissions.

today: RFC 967 proposes a subseries of essays about integrating networking code into operating systems. The memo invites volunteers and offers coordination.

sections.title: A Gap in Networking Literature
sections.content:
The author observes that operating-system vendors and networking implementers had difficulties over changes needed for networking. The RFC argues that the literature had not addressed this issue directly enough.

The author says the literature is a way for researchers to educate practitioners and proposes adding documentation about integration work.
sections.plainLanguage: Networking may require operating-system changes, but the author says the community has not written enough about how those changes are made. This memo proposes filling that gap.

sections.title: Proposed OS Integration Essays
sections.content:
The proposed subseries would collect short essays from people who integrated network code with different operating systems. Each essay should discuss Host-Host protocol interpreters, the host-communications subnet processor and any device driver, Telnet, FTP, and relevant operating-system structure.

The author offers to coordinate submissions and says separate contributions about the same system might be combined.
sections.plainLanguage: Each essay would explain how a particular operating system handles network protocols and related software. Contributors could coordinate when they cover the same system.

sections.title: Scope of the Call
sections.content:
The author hopes volunteers will cover major operating systems on the network and most minor ones. The stated goal is a collection that can help practitioners understand the work needed to integrate networking.

The memo invites the RFC community to consider the proposal and volunteer contributions.
sections.plainLanguage: The author invites implementers to describe networking support across many operating systems. The proposal is a call for documentation and contributions.
